note: Literature reports confirm that brain iron accumulation in GTPBP2-related disorder is age-dependent and frequently undetectable in infancy and childhood.

evidence.text: In GTPBP2-associated neuro-ectodermal syndrome, clinical findings show that brain iron accumulation is age-dependent and may only become apparent after childhood.

source.title: Clinical delineation of GTPBP2‐associated neuro‐ectodermal syndrome: Report of two new families and review of the literature
source.quote: Our findings suggest that some aspects of the clinical presentation appear to be age-related; brain iron accumulation may appear only after childhood, and the ectodermal findings and peripheral neuropathy are most prominent in older individuals.

evidence.text: Review of neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation indicates that disorders such as GTPBP2-related disease can present or occur without early basal ganglia iron accumulation.
